newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA unsure of strike effect on France cargo.
newsitem.headline: BA unsure of strike effect on France cargo.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo said it would not have a complete picture on the impact of the cabin crew strike on its freight operations in France until later on Wednesday.

"We were fully-prepared for the strike, having notified our French agent customers by letter in good time and putting contingency plans in place. We won't know until this evening where we stand exactly," Friedrich Wendler, BA's cargo director, Western Europe, told Reuters.

BA flights between Paris and London had been badly affected by the strike but the airline was maintaining nightly cargo trucking runs between Paris-CDG and London Heathrow and Gatwick airports, a BA Paris-based cargo official said.
Meanwhile, at Nice, from where BA operates two daily flights to Heathrow and two to Gatwick, cargo had been flown out near-normally today, Air Azur, BA's local cargo handling agent, told Reuters.
"Only one of these four flights -- departing late afternoon to Heathrow and using a Boeing 767 -- carries freight," an Air Azur spokesman said.
"Because of the strike, we put the cargo on the early afternoon 767 flight (to give more time for arriving consignments to be offloaded and accepted by forwarders)," he added.
The 767 flight is a major BA cargo asset in southern France as it has a capacity to carry up to 13 tonnes of palletised freight per flight.

At Lyon, another of BA's major provincial centres in France, the cancellation of a daily service to Heathrow because of the cabin crew strike, saw the airline truck cargo to Geneva, from where it operates a 767 flight to London.
Freight was also being trucked from the Lyon area ,to London, a BA cargo official in Lyon said.
